question: A cocktail glass is a cone, point down. Filled to half its height, what fraction of the full glass holds drink?
answer: An eighth. The drink is a smaller cone of the same shape, half as tall and half as wide, so its volume is ½ × ½ × ½ = ⅛. Fill to three-quarters of the height and it still holds only about 42%: 0.75³. Euclid proved similar cones scale by the cube.
move: Similar shapes scale their volume by the cube of their size.
ask: Which half-full container have I misjudged by looking at its height?
trap: A half, since the drink reaches half the height.
